$comment: TELEMETRY RETENTION AND SAMPLING. The workspace half of FR-OPS-011 and FR-OPS-012.
The application configures what it can (ragcore/src/ragcore/observability/) and this file
configures what only the workspace can. Both halves are needed, and the application half is
the weaker one: a workspace quietly retaining telemetry for two years would defeat FR-OPS-004
from outside the application, with nothing in the codebase to show for it.
WHY RETENTION IS A CONTROL AND NOT A COST DECISION. Telemetry MUST NOT answer a question audit
is responsible for (FR-OPS-004). That is unenforceable as a rule about intent - somebody will
always be able to answer an audit question from a trace if the trace is still there. Thirty
days against audit's seven years makes it enforceable as a matter of fact: after a month the
question demonstrably cannot be answered from here, whatever anybody intended.
WHY SAMPLING IS TAIL-BASED. A journey suspends for a human decision and resumes hours later in
a different process. Head sampling decides at the first span, before the journey is known to be
interesting, and routinely keeps the request half of an approval and discards the resume half -
which defeats SC-OPS-001 exactly. It is prohibited here rather than merely discouraged.
Thirty days, and the application reports the same number from SYNTHIA_OTEL_RETENTION_DAYS.
ragcore/tests/unit/test_settings.py asserts the two agree, because two places holding the
same number is two places for them to stop agreeing - and the drift would be invisible.
The 'class-based mechanism' FR-OPS-011 refers to is the same one governing every other data
class (data-model.md retention classes). Telemetry is one class among several; it is not a
special case with its own lifecycle.

contrastWith.why: The gap is the control. See FR-OPS-004 and FR-AUDIT-004.

$comment: TWO LAYERS, and neither is sufficient alone.
In-process (CorrelationJourneySampler) makes the decision CONSISTENT: it is derived from the
correlation identifier, so every span of one journey reaches the same answer independently,
in processes that never spoke to each other and hours apart. That is what makes the
suspend-and-resume case work without coordination.
In the collector, tail sampling makes the decision INFORMED: it happens after the spans are
in, so 'this journey contained an error' is a fact rather than a prediction.
The in-process layer exists so the collector is never handed a half-sampled journey, which it
could not repair.
Retained whatever the ratio says. Each entry is a thing an operator goes looking for, and
a sampled-away denial is a question that cannot be answered at all - unlike a sampled-away
successful request, which is one of thousands that look the same.
The application marks these with the synthia.retain span attribute
(ragcore/src/ragcore/observability/sampling.py), so the two layers agree on what counts as
interesting rather than each deciding separately.

conditions.why: A trace nobody kept is a failure nobody can explain.
The record of the platform refusing something. Never ordinary.
A human decided. The journey around that decision is the one that gets reviewed.

ordinaryJourneyRatio.$comment: Applies ONLY to journeys carrying none of the conditions above. A low value here discards the ordinary and nothing else.

$comment: Entra-authenticated ingestion, so the connection string contributes the ENDPOINT rather than
the AUTHORITY. The instrumentation key inside a connection string is a write credential for
the workspace: hold it and you can inject telemetry into somebody else's dashboards. It is
therefore a Key Vault reference in both container manifests and never a plain value.
The role is Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the workspace, held by both deployables
(build/infra/identity/managed-identities.json). Publisher, not Contributor: neither
deployable reads telemetry back, and neither configures the workspace.
WHAT MUST NEVER REACH A SINK (plan Stage 10 security). Enforced in the application by
ragcore/src/ragcore/observability/logging.py - a redacting filter on every record, plus a
formatter with an ALLOW-LIST of fields, so an attribute nobody named is not serialised at
all. Asserted by ragcore/tests/security/test_no_leakage.py.
Listed here as well because the workspace is the other end of the same pipe, and a diagnostic
setting added there could re-open what the application closed.
permittedIdentifiers: the platform tenant_id, as a dimension
opaque platform identifiers (session, work item, operation)
